question.text: The requirement that Investment Committee members be responsible for compliance with SEBI (AIF) Regulations under the 2021 amendment does NOT apply to which of the following fund types?

answer.text: All Category I AIFs regardless of investor profile
Only angel funds registered as sub-category of Cat I AIF
Only Category III AIFs with AUM above INR 500 crore

Large Value Funds for Accredited Investors and AIFs where each investor (other than Manager, Sponsor, and employees/directors of the AIF/Investment Manager) has committed at least INR 70 crore and furnished a waiver

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Ch 11.7.3, the requirement that IC members shall be responsible for compliance does NOT apply to (a) Large Value Funds for Accredited Investors and (b) AIFs where each investor (other than Manager, Sponsor, and employees/directors of the AIF/Investment Manager) has committed minimum INR 70 crore or equivalent and has furnished a waiver to the AIF. Reference: SEBI Circular dated June 25, 2021. The Trap: Option A is too broad — Category I is not wholesale exempt. Option B misidentifies angel funds, which do follow the requirement. Option C invents an AUM threshold. Note: The carve-out covers LVFs and INR 70 crore-plus committed investors, with the Manager/Sponsor/employees/directors exclusion from the per-investor commitment test.
